info.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 25 at 3:27AM MDT until September 25 at 7:30AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
info.description:
At 327 AM MDT, Another round of heavier rainfall is moving into the southern Sacramento Mountains with rainfall rates of 0.50 to 1 inch per hour over a broad, saturated area in complex terrain.
HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing flash flooding.
SOURCE...Radar and rain gauge indicated.
IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.
Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Sacramento, Mayhill, Weed, Sixteen Springs, James Canyon, Cox Canyon and Hay Canyon.
Thunderstorms extend from Mayhill to Sunspot, and out over the Tularosa Basin. Rainfall rates of up to 1 inch per hour have been observed in heavier downpours north of Timberon and near Mayhill.
This includes the following streams and drainages... Rio Penasco, Agua Chiquita Creek, Bluewater Creek, Dry Burnt Canyon, Elk Canyon, Lower Portions of Hay Canyon, Cox Canyon, and James Canyon.
The most serious flooding impacts will be in downstream locations including Mayhill, Sacramento, and Weed.
There are some signs that precipitation will begin to diminish between 4 AM and 5 AM, but runoff will continue for some time afterwards.
info.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the dangers of flooding.
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law enforcement.
